headline: Your D-ID waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing marketing, L&D, CX, and sales-enablement buyers into the right D-ID Video Studio, Visual AI Agent, or competitor-switch offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Nader Wahba, VP Sales, North America.
productSummary: D-ID (d-id.com) is an enterprise AI visual-agents and generative video platform. Homepage positioning: AI videos and interactive avatars for humanlike communication — explain clearly, engage personally, and scale messaging across every audience and channel. Core products on d-id.com: Video Studio (polished multilingual avatar videos from scripts, briefs, decks, or documents); Visual AI Agents (real-time conversational avatars that engage face-to-face, trigger workflows, and run in multiple languages, fully embeddable); AI Avatars (digital humans from images or video with voice cloning for offline video and real-time experiences). Published capabilities: brand-adaptable avatars, 120+ languages, API / real-time streaming (WebRTC Client SDK), RAG knowledge bases, configurable LLMs (built-in, external keys, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints), PowerPoint / Canva / Google Slides integrations, enterprise security and permissions. Buyer teams named on site: Marketing, Learning & Development, Sales Enablement, Customer Experience, Content Creators, and Developers. March 2026 public proof: V4 Expressive Visual Agents for low-latency LLM-connected conversations; D-ID claims 1,500+ enterprise customers, 800,000+ visual agents and 300M+ non-interactive avatars created on prior models; September 2025 acquisition of simpleshow (explainer video). Nader Wahba is VP of Sales, North America (nader.wahba@d-id.com).
coreInsight: Nader sells one D-ID digital-human platform — Video Studio + Visual AI Agents + AI Avatars — not a different product per vertical. Marketing vs L&D vs CX vs sales enablement is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall. The single routing signal is ai_avatar_maturity: what a lead source can already see about how they produce talking-head or interactive experiences — competing AI avatar/video platform, heavy filmed video production without an AI avatar tool, conversational AI / chatbot without a face, or none. That ladder maps to D-ID's live offers: competitor switch into V4 real-time agents + Studio, replace costly video production with Studio avatars, overlay a Visual AI Agent on existing LLM/chat, then a soft remaining-TAM Visual Agents playbook.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how far their AI talking-head stack already shows up publicly
sections.takeaway: BuiltWith, site widgets, careers, and LMS/marketing pages already show a competing AI avatar tool, heavy filmed video production, a text chatbot without a face, or none. That ai_avatar_maturity is stronger than a title guess and cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM marketing, L&D, CX, and sales account
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Competitor AI avatar platform first, then filmed-production-without-AI-avatar, then chatbot-without-visual-agent, then every remaining in-TAM buyer.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each maturity band gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Competitor platforms get a Switch + Real-Time Agents Brief. Filmed-production accounts get a Video Studio Replace Production Brief. Chatbot-only accounts get a Visual AI Agent Overlay Brief. The rest get the D-ID Visual Agents Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the stack, replace the studio, add a face, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always accounts D-ID sells into (marketing, L&D, CX, sales enablement, developer platforms). Segment is a merge tag. A/Bs sit on exclusive routes (real-time agents vs Studio cost, production-hours vs multilingual scale).

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the avatar or chat signal already visible on their stack
sections.takeaway: Notice the competitor, filmed production, or chatbot, poke the production / latency / face-less gap that state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competitor-platform switch route first
sections.takeaway: Start where ai_avatar_maturity already shows HeyGen, Synthesia, Colossyan, Hour One, Elai, Tavus, or similar. Prove reply density, then roll Replace Production, Visual Agent Overlay, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Apollo / LinkedIn Sales Nav (Marketing, L&D, CX, Sales Enablement, Product titles at mid-market and enterprise) are the TAM D-ID already sells into. Public global TAM account count is not published on d-id.com; treat size as estimated (see d-id-magnet-flags.txt) and keep each launch tier >=~1,500 contacts where possible.

The same BuiltWith + site + careers scrape returns ai_avatar_maturity: competing AI avatar/video platforms (HeyGen, Synthesia, Colossyan, Hour One, Elai, Tavus, adjacent); heavy filmed video / instructional-design production without an AI avatar tool; conversational AI / chatbot widgets (Intercom, Drift, Zendesk, custom) without a visual agent; or none — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live D-ID positioning (Video Studio, V4 Expressive Visual Agents, AI Avatars, 120+ languages, API / WebRTC Client SDK, RAG + configurable LLMs, PowerPoint/Canva/Slides) plus public proof language (SPIN Sport Innovation, SingIt, Defined AI, Pitango, MyHeritage, simpleshow acquisition footprint).

Segment (marketing vs L&D vs CX vs sales enablement vs developers) and use case (training, support, website concierge, demos) are scrape filters and merge tags, not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the account is routed.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND ai_avatar_maturity = competitor_platform (HeyGen, Synthesia, Colossyan, Hour One, Elai, Tavus, or adjacent AI avatar/talking-head video tool) AND not already_customer
routingRules.then: Tier 1 - Competitor Switch + Real-Time Agents Brief
routingRules.why: They already budget an AI avatar / talking-head stack. Strongest switch intent for D-ID as the real-time Visual Agents + Studio platform (V4 latency, API, 120+ languages) versus pre-recorded-first competitors.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND ai_avatar_maturity = filmed_production_no_avatar (video producer / instructional designer / studio roles OR human-presenter training/marketing video library) AND no Tier-1 competitor_platform AND not already_customer
routingRules.then: Tier 2 - Video Studio Replace Production Brief
routingRules.why: They still shoot or hire for talking-head content at scale. Maps to D-ID Video Studio: minutes-not-days avatar videos from scripts/decks, brand-adaptable, multilingual — without inventing an AI tool they do not have.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND ai_avatar_maturity = chat_no_visual_agent (Intercom / Drift / Zendesk chat / custom conversational AI on site or product) AND no Tier 1-2 AND not already_customer
routingRules.then: Tier 3 - Visual AI Agent Overlay Brief
routingRules.why: They already run text or voice chat but no face. Maps to D-ID Visual AI Agents: LLM-connected, RAG-grounded, WebRTC-streamed digital humans for CX, website concierge, or training roleplay.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (marketing, L&D, CX, sales enablement, developer platforms). Softest CTA around AI video + interactive agents. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1

tiers.pain: They are already paying for an AI avatar or talking-head stack optimized for pre-recorded clips — and still lack low-latency, LLM-connected face-to-face agents for CX, website, or interactive training.
tiers.valueProp: Competitor Switch + Real-Time Agents Brief: D-ID as the V4 Visual Agents + Video Studio platform — sub-second conversational avatars, API/WebRTC, 120+ languages, RAG + configurable LLMs.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Filmed video production, no AI avatar tool
tiers.trigger: ai_avatar_maturity = filmed_production_no_avatar (video producer / instructional designer / studio roles OR human-presenter training/marketing video library); no Tier-1 competitor_platform

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Conversational AI / chatbot, no visual agent
tiers.trigger: ai_avatar_maturity = chat_no_visual_agent (Intercom / Drift / Zendesk chat / custom conversational AI) with no Tier 1-2 match
tiers.pain: Text chat answers questions but feels faceless — drop-off on complex CX, onboarding, and sales-qualification flows where tone and presence matter.
tiers.valueProp: Visual AI Agent Overlay Brief: put a D-ID V4 Expressive Visual Agent on the existing LLM/knowledge stack — real-time WebRTC face, RAG answers, exportable conversation logs.
tiers.dataSource: Site widget / support-page scrape for chat stacks
tiers.replyDensity: Medium - clear chat stack, education on visual agents

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM marketing / L&D / CX / sales accounts

tiers.pain: Most mid-market and enterprise teams know video and always-on digital presence are coming — but have not publicly exposed an AI avatar tool, filmed-production org, or chatbot widget yet.
tiers.valueProp: Soft D-ID Visual Agents Playbook: practical paths into Video Studio, real-time Visual AI Agents, and multilingual avatars — soft CTA, site proof of V4 + 120+ languages + enterprise API.

launchPlan: Suppress visible D-ID customers first when Nader's team can share a customer list.
Launch Tier 1 Competitor Switch + Real-Time Agents Brief; hold until >=~1,500 contacts when TAM allows, else run smaller waves with longer reply-density read.
Roll Tier 2 Video Studio Replace Production Brief (A/B production-hours vs multilingual scale), then Tier 3 Visual AI Agent Overlay Brief.
Open Catch-all D-ID Visual Agents Playbook for remaining TAM.
A/B inside exclusive routes: real-time agents vs Studio cost (Tier 1); hours saved vs {{language_count}} languages (Tier 2); CX triage vs website concierge (Tier 3).
Keep segment (marketing vs L&D vs CX vs sales enablement vs developers) and use case as merge tags only — do not split into parallel waterfalls per vertical.
